Full-season model decisions

The 2024 and 2025 seasons select the models, including their playoff games. The 2026 test now includes the Cincinnati–Pittsburgh final. Each fixed policy faces the same final game IDs for its supported targets.

2852024 validation finals
2852025 validation finals

The market remains the operational incumbent. The validation results below nominate research models for individual targets. Selection weights are 30% for 2024 and 70% for 2025. Earlier releases had already examined 2026 results. The Pittsburgh final updates test performance only.

Validation leaders across forecast protocols

The opening moneyline leads on decisive-winner log loss and Brier. A 50/50 blend of the market and N110 leads the three-way winner scores. N110 with an opening-line fallback leads margin MAE. The last archived DraftKings total leads total MAE and RMSE. The clocks below show which information each policy had.

Browse every registered model, metric and coverage gap
What goes into each model?
ModelFeatures and fitting
N123 integer calibrationStarts from N122 league/home. Uses preceding-season residuals to recalibrate the probability at each integer margin and total, including ties and key scoring margins.
N113 team strengthAway-minus-home differences in recent points scored and allowed, last-eight opponent net strength, last-16 team net strength, and capped rest.
N121 recent / pooled opponent ridgeTeam offense, opposing defense, home advantage and league scoring. Recent uses a 140-day half-life and ridge penalty 6. Pooled uses 330 days and penalty 12.
N025 retained historical ensembleSeven component forecasts for winner and margin; six for total. Includes scoring, points allowed, opponent strength, count models and prior out-of-fold forecast errors.
Dated quarterback modelWeekly team and starting-quarterback effects from dated pregame depth charts. Unknown starters retain the team-level estimate.
N110 with opening-market fallbackUses the N110 model where a time-qualified forecast is available, with the dated opening line supplying an explicit fallback elsewhere.

Circa five-pick cards

Each official contest week allows five distinct selections. The ranking uses P(cover) + 0.5 × P(push). A winning side earns one point, a push earns half a point, and a loss earns zero.

Two policies tied on both validation seasons, with 45/90 points in 2024 and 47/90 in 2025. The preregistered primary policy calibrated both cover direction and pushes. Its 2026 card earned 19 points from 49 settled selections, with Baltimore −4.5 still open. The direction-only policy earned 20/49 with one open.

All 15 policies face the same 46 official worksheets. The 2026 closed-week column gives each policy exactly nine weeks and 45 settled slots. All 690 cards are research reconstructions. No contest submission receipt was found.

Upcoming games

Five fresh fits produced 615 projections for 123 unstarted fixtures, 99 timed and 24 with kickoff TBD. The models use the Pittsburgh final and the source as of 10:35 a.m. Pacific. Monday forecasts were computed at 10:48 a.m. Pacific. Sunday forecasts are retained for comparison. Each forecast retains its computation and issue history. Later games can still have intervening team results or lineup changes.

Monday margin and total probabilities

The margin is away points minus home points. For an away side at −3, enter 3. A margin above 3 covers, exactly 3 pushes, and below 3 loses. Half-point thresholds have zero push probability.
